summary: Four added Scaladoc entries make false representation or hash-contract claims; the diff is otherwise comment-only.

items.issue: The comment promises a new bitset, but the delegated factory returns `coll` unchanged when it is already an immutable `BitSet`.
items.suggestion: Say it returns a bitset containing `coll`'s elements and note that an existing immutable bitset is returned unchanged.

items.issue: The wrapper is documented as directly backing the result with `elems`, but the delegated factory retains the array only when it has more than two words. Empty and small inputs use canonical/word-field representations instead.
items.suggestion: Qualify the backing-array claim for arrays with more than two words, or describe only the bit contents.

items.issue: The comment says the mutable builder's word array becomes the result's backing array without copying. That only holds for results with more than two words; empty and small bitsets use canonical/`BitSet1`/`BitSet2` representations.
items.suggestion: Qualify the backing-array claim for results with more than two words, or remove the representation-detail paragraph.

items.issue: This is not a Java `Set`-contract hash: implementations accumulate improved hashes (`Hashing.improve(key.##)`), while the Java/Scala set hash contract uses ordinary element hash codes. It is also computed on demand in hash-collision nodes rather than universally cached.
items.suggestion: Describe it as the sum of improved hashes used internally for trie equality/fast rejection, without claiming the Java `Set` contract or universal caching.
